items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to criminal history of transportation network company drivers; and to amend the criminal procedure law, in relation to sealing of certain convictions
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6631

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to criminal
history of transportation network company drivers; and to amend the
criminal procedure law, in relation to sealing of certain convictions

 PURPOSE OF BILL :

This bill would clarify two provisions enacted as part of Chapter 59
of 2017. First, the bill would clarify that persons required to
register as a sex offender are not eligible for a transportation
network company (TNC) permit. Second, the bill would also clarify that
only one application for the sealing of criminal records must be filed
and fix a typographical error.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS OF BILL :

Sections 1 and 2 clarify that persons required to register as a sex
offender are not eligible to receive a permit to drive a car for a
TNC.

Section 3 of clarifies that person applying for sealing of their
criminal records, pursuant to provisions of law enacted in the SFY
2017-18 budget, are only required to file one application.

Section 4 of the bill fixes a typographical error in the provisions of
law dealing with applications to seal certain criminal records.

Section 5 is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

There has been concern expressed that the legislation enacted as part
of Chapter 59 of 2017 (SFY 2017-18 enacted budget) to permit TNCs to
operate in New York was not clear that persons required to register as
sex offenders are not eligible for TNC permits. Therefore, this
legislation clarifies the law to clearly provide that persons required
to register as sex offenders are disqualified from driving for a TNC.

Also, such Chapter 59 of 2017 included a provision of law that allows
for the sealing of certain, non-violent criminal records. The
legislation allows for up to two convictions (no more than one felony)
to be sealed by a court upon application. However, there is some
conflicting language about the filing of an application for a person
seeking to seal two convictions and whether multiple applications are
required in such circumstance. Therefore, this bill clarifies that
only one application is necessary. Further, the bill fixes a
typographical error in the legislation regarding the waiver of the
ability to apply for sealing.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This Act will take effect immediately, provided, however, that
sections one and two of this act shall take effect on the same date
and in the same manner as section 2 of part AAA of chapter 59 of the
laws of 2017, takes effect; provided further that sections three and
four of this act shall take effect on the same date and in the same
manner as section 48 of part WWW of chapter 59 of the laws of 2017,
takes effect.
